subject: Environment access ownership & deployment gate for Aurora Health private stack
messages:
From: J. Reed <jreed@aurorahealth.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@aurorahealth.com
Date: 2026-09-12T08:15:00-07:00
Subject: Ownership of environment access + deployment gate for private stack

Hi Lauren,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. Before we lock in timelines for the private VPC deployment, security wants a short doc that names owners for these items and confirms the pre-deploy gate checklist we need to satisfy:

- Account-level IAM ownership (who in Aurora approves service account creation)
- Network egress/ingress ports and required CIDR allowlists
- KMS key custody and rotation responsibilities
- Audit log retention and where logs will be shipped (splunk vs. RH audit bucket)
- Who signs off on the final pre-production runbook

Can Redwood map the Redwood-owned vs Aurora-owned responsibilities and confirm whether Redwood needs any elevated access during the first deploy window? Procurement is copied for scheduling and any contract notes.

Best,
Jared Reed
Director, Infrastructure
Aurora Health

--
Attachment: requirements_from_aurora.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
To: J. Reed <jreed@aurorahealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, dev_patel@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-12T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Ownership of environment access + deployment gate for private stack

Hi Jared,

Thanks for laying this out — good checklist. I attached a concise Redwood pre-deploy checklist and an ownership matrix (redwood_onboard_prereqs.pdf) that splits responsibilities into "Redwood operational tasks" and "Aurora tasks / approvals." High-level answers below; the PDF has the detailed runbook items.

- Account-level IAM: Aurora approves all production service accounts. Redwood will propose service-account names and the least-privilege IAM policy; Aurora infra will create the accounts or give a service-account creation window. (Owner: Aurora infra)
- Network ports / allowlists: Redwood needs TCP 443 outbound and a small set of ingress ranges for our bastion and control-plane. We provide a port-matrix and test CIDR (attached in CSV). Temporary host-level SSH will be blocked except via our jump host; we'll request an approved user list. (Owner: joint — Redwood defines ports; Aurora applies allowlist)
- KMS custody: For customer-managed KMS, Aurora holds the key; Redwood integrates via cross-account grant. If customer prefers Redwood-managed key, we require an ACL and rotation policy. (Owner: Aurora primary)
- Audit logs: Default is ship to Aurora-owned S3 long-term bucket (30-90d retention configurable). Redwood can mirror logs to our audit store for 14d if requested.
- Sign-off: Aurora sec + Aurora infra sign off on pre-prod smoke run; Redwood will provide runbook and test checklist.

Next steps:
1) Dev, can you attach the port matrix and call out any special network tests we should schedule for the first deployment?
2) Jared, if Aurora can confirm the name of the S3 bucket and KMS ARN by EOD Thursday, we can lock the first deploy window for the week of 9/21.

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0114

--
Attachment: redwood_onboard_prereqs.pdf (summary checklist)

From: dev_patel@redwood.com
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-13T09:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Ownership of environment access + deployment gate for private stack

Added technical detail / action items for the port/CIDR and preflight tests below — pulling from our standard private deploy playbook. I attached the port-matrix.csv export for Aurora infra to import into their firewall ticketing system.

- Required outbound ports: 443 (control plane), 50051 (gRPC metrics, optional, can be tunneled), 80 (healthcheck redirect only).
- Inbound: only our bastion public IPs (we will use ephemeral egress IPs; list in the port matrix).
- Healthcheck endpoints: /_healthz (443) and /v1/status (443) — smoke tests will exercise both.
- KV cache persistence: confirm NFS/EBS mount permissions for checkpointing if using on-prem nodes. Owner: Aurora infra to ensure mount options and uid/gid mapping.
- KMS: we require Encrypt/Decrypt/GenerateDataKey permissions for the service account. If Aurora uses HSM-backed keys, we need the signer grant.
- Test runbook: preflight (port ping, TLS handshake, KMS key test), canary deploy (single node), traffic soak (2h), rollback plan.

Action items (Dev):
- I will provide a small terraform snippet for the service-account policy and a short script to validate the KMS grant.
- Marissa: can you confirm whether we need a separate CIDR for canary traffic so Aurora can route it to the staging VPC?

Attachments: port-matrix.csv (CSV stub)

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
dev_patel@redwood.com

Lauren / team —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the ownership matrix. Two quick confirmations from our side:

1) Bucket and KMS: aurora-logs-prod (s3://aurora-logs-prod) and KMS ARN: arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/abcd-ef01-2345. Security says we will grant the cross-account Encrypt/Decrypt/GenerateDataKey permissions by end of day Friday.

2) CIDR: we'll create a temporary CIDR pool 10.250.100.0/26 for your canary traffic and will append the port matrix into Jira ticket INFRA-7832.

If you can drop the terraform snippet and the KMS validation script into the Drive link you provided, we can schedule the canary deploy for 9/22 morning. Procurement will follow up on the contract amendment for the dedicated capacity SLA.

-Jared
